summary: A two-line fix to release tooling. At the base, bumpCargoPackageVersion detected a missing [package] version line by checking whether the replace changed the text, so it also threw when the crate version already equalled the target. The crate and @cipherstash/eql are both at 3.0.5 at head, so every `pnpm run version` that does not bump EQL would have stopped the whole release after `changeset version` had already rewritten the tree. The head checks for the version line directly and returns the manifest unchanged on a no-op, while still throwing when the line is missing. The fix is narrow and correct as read, and the new unit test runs in the `Run Tests (Node 22/24)` CI jobs, which passed. The residual risk is that a no-EQL-bump release now gets past step 2 for the first time and reaches the Cargo.lock refresh and the skew-gated SQL asset step. Those steps are unit-tested with injected runners but have not been run for real on an unchanged version. Any failure there fails closed: the release job stops and needs a fix and a re-run. It cannot publish wrong artefacts. Nothing touches encryption, payloads or published library code.

behaviour_changes.description: bumpCargoPackageVersion no longer throws when the [package] version already equals the target; it returns the Cargo.toml text unchanged. A [package] section with no `version = "..."` line still throws the same error, now from an explicit regex test before the replace.

The root `version` script (`changeset version && node scripts/sync-lockstep-versions.mjs`), run by changesets/action in release.yml, now completes step 2 on releases that do not bump @cipherstash/eql. It then goes on to step 3 (`mise exec -- cargo update --package eql-bindings` for every Cargo.lock that records the crate by path) and step 4 (prepareBindingAssets, which skips the rebuild when eqlLockstepSkew finds no skew). At the base these releases stopped at step 2.
Adds a unit test asserting that bumpCargoPackageVersion(CARGO, '0.4.2') returns CARGO unchanged. The existing test that a missing version line throws is kept.

affected_components.name: Root `version` script and the release.yml changesets/action `version:` step
affected_components.how: package.json `version` chains the script after `changeset version`; release.yml runs `pnpm run version` through changesets/action. Every release goes through it.

affected_components.name: eql-bindings crate manifest and the Cargo.lock files that record it by path (packages/eql, packages/protect-ffi)
affected_components.how: main() writes the function's output back to packages/eql/crates/eql-bindings/Cargo.toml and then refreshes each discovered Cargo.lock. On a no-EQL-bump release these refreshes now run where they previously never ran.

affected_components.name: EQL SQL bundle and release manifests (prepareBindingAssets / eqlLockstepSkew)
affected_components.how: Step 4 is now reached on no-EQL-bump releases. It skips when eqlLockstepSkew finds nothing; otherwise it rebuilds, which the gate rejects as frozen-bytes-skew if the bytes differ.

failure_scenarios.title: First no-EQL-bump release runs the lock-refresh and asset steps for real and stops the release
failure_scenarios.trigger: The first stack release after this merges that does not bump @cipherstash/eql (the PR says this is every release after EQL 3.0.6).
failure_scenarios.mechanism: At the base, the throw at step 2 meant steps 3 and 4 had only ever run on releases where the EQL version moved. Now main() continues to cargoLockWorkspaces, `mise exec -- cargo update --package eql-bindings` per workspace (not offline, in a job with a cold registry), and prepareBindingAssets. If any of these misbehaves on an unchanged version, the hook throws or the gate fails closed: a cargo resolution error, a non-empty eqlLockstepSkew from tree skew that triggers a rebuild, or a rebuild whose digest differs and fires frozen-bytes-skew.
failure_scenarios.consequence: The release job fails after `changeset version` has rewritten manifests and changelogs in the CI checkout. No package is published wrongly, but the release is blocked until a fix lands and the job re-runs. This is the same class of outcome the PR removes, now possible one step later.

evidence.claim: Head tests for the version line explicitly (throws if absent), then replaces and returns; no throw when the replacement is identical.
Base throws 'did not find a version line' whenever `updated === packageSection[0]`, which includes an unchanged version.
The crate [package] version is 3.0.5, equal to packages/eql/packages/eql/package.json version 3.0.5, so a run without an EQL bump hits the no-op case.
main() writes the bump result, then refreshes every discovered Cargo.lock via cargo update, then calls prepareBindingAssets.
Root `version` script is `changeset version && node scripts/sync-lockstep-versions.mjs`.
changesets/action runs `version: pnpm run version`, so the hook runs on every release.

prepareBindingAssets skips when eqlLockstepSkew is empty, otherwise runs the mise rebuild and throws if skew remains; the comment explains that a rebuilt digest under an unchanged version trips frozen-bytes-skew in the gate.
The existing missing-version-line throw test remains; the new test asserts unchanged output for a matching version.
pr-description.md: PR states every stack release after EQL 3.0.6 leaves EQL's version alone and would hit this path.
The Run Tests (Node matrix) job runs `pnpm run test:scripts`, which covers scripts/__tests__.
